title: A Record 168, and Four Holes That Settled It: John Patterson Wins TEG 9
title_candidates: A Record 168, and Four Holes That Settled It: John Patterson Wins TEG 9
Level at the 14th: John Patterson Holds Off Alex Baker for the TEG 9 Trophy
Highs and Horrors on the Lisbon Coast: Patterson's 168, Mullin's Course Record, Alex Baker's 115
Two Best-in-Field Rounds: How John Patterson Posted the Biggest Trophy Total TEG Has Seen
theme: A tournament of violent swings — the highest Trophy total in TEG history, the second-best round ever, a new course record and a new course-worst all from the same six men on the same two courses — won by the player whose peaks landed on the right days, while the only metronome in the field quietly took the Jacket.
tone: house — subverted gravitas, British English, tongue-in-cheek but exact; restraint and specific numbers, escalation reserved for the blow-ups
opening_hook: Open at the 14th at Praia D'El Rey in R4, with Alex Baker level with John Patterson and four holes to play — the tournament genuinely tied at that instant — then rewind, because the round that actually won it had been played two rounds earlier.

trophy_storyline.subject: John Patterson's record 168: two best-in-field rounds either side of an R3 wobble that let Alex Baker draw level with four holes left
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: It is the highest Trophy total TEG has recorded, and despite the six-point margin the outcome was genuinely level with four holes of the tournament remaining.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: a first-ever look at Royal Óbidos produced 38 points and a sextuple-bogey 10 at the SI-1 4th (b61), leaving Patterson one behind Jon Baker after R1. Turn: 49 points at Praia D'El Rey in R2 — the second-best round in TEG history (b08), 17 of them across holes 9-13 (b44) — put him ten clear, before a 34 in R3 (b49), his only round in the bottom half, cut the lead to three and set up a last-round scrap. Resolution: Alex Baker drew level at the 14th in R4 and then bled 11 shots over 14-17 (b16) while Patterson answered with 47, best in the field again (b45), for 168 and a personal-best gross total of +88 (b34, b38, b01).

trophy_storyline.chosen_headline: John Patterson's 168 Sets a TEG Record
trophy_storyline.standfirst: Best-in-field rounds of 49 and 47 at Praia D'El Rey framed a Round 3 stumble that let Alex Baker level the TEG 9 Trophy with four holes left to play.

jacket_storyline.subject: David Mullin's seventh Green Jacket: best in the field in all four rounds, a new Royal Óbidos course record, and Jon Baker's career-best gross beaten by ten
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: Mullin's +67 is the lowest gross total in TEG history, won with a Jacket lead he held from the first round to the last, in a competition he has now won in each of the last four TEGs as well.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: Mullin opened with 87 gross at Royal Óbidos — a new course record, beating the previous mark of 90 set across six prior visits (cr01) — and by the 18th of R1 the gross lead was his outright and never changed hands again. Turn: the only threats came from his own card, a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 10th in R3 (b15) and a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 1st in R4 (b17), each answered immediately — three untroubled pars at 2-4 and nine points from 7-9 in R4 (b40, b21, b23). Resolution: best in the field in all four rounds, +67 by ten (b04), with Jon Baker posting the best gross total of his career, +77, and finishing nowhere near him (b33, b25).

jacket_storyline.chosen_headline: David Mullin's Course Record Kills the Jacket Race
jacket_storyline.standfirst: His 87 at Royal Óbidos in Round 1 broke a mark that had stood through six visits and handed him a gross lead nobody touched — Jon Baker's career-best +77 finished ten adrift.

spoon_storyline.subject: Stuart Neumann's back-to-back Wooden Spoon: bottom of the field after all four rounds and 16 adrift, despite improving every time out
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: He arrived as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder and never once climbed off the bottom of the TEG 9 Trophy table, finishing 16 points behind Gregg Williams, the next man up.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: 23 points and +42 gross at Royal Óbidos in R1, a round in which his front nine beat his back nine by 11 points (b50); he was bottom of the Spoon race by the 15th and stayed there for the rest of the tournament. Turn: he then got steadily better — 30, then 37 in R3, with nine points across 6-8 and twelve across 10-13 (b43, b24), and a new personal best at Royal Óbidos of 98 gross, an improvement of exactly one shot. Resolution: R4 brought the best golf of his tournament, 16 points across 11-15 including a birdie at the 13th and four holes without dropping a gross shot (b07, b11) — before an 8 at the 16th and a ruinous walk in; 127 points, and a second Spoon in a row (b39).
headline_candidates: Stuart Neumann Improves Daily, Finishes Last Anyway

spoon_storyline.chosen_headline: Stuart Neumann Improves Daily, Finishes Last Anyway
spoon_storyline.standfirst: The reigning Wooden Spoon holder climbed from 23 points to 37, set a personal best at Royal Óbidos and still ended TEG 9 sixteen points behind the next man up.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker goes from a Royal Óbidos course-worst 115 to twin personal-best 44-point rounds at Praia D'El Rey and second in the Trophy
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The man who posted the worst gross round ever recorded at Royal Óbidos finished runner-up with the best gross total of his career, and was level for the lead with four holes to play.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 was 115 gross at Royal Óbidos, a new course-worst beating the previous 108 across six prior visits (cr02), his own worst gross round to date at +43 (b37), complete with a septuple-bogey 11 at the 14th (b18) and a quintuple-bogey 9 at the SI-2 12th (b29) — and bottom of the Spoon race by the 2nd. Turn: at Praia D'El Rey in R2 he posted 44 points and +27 gross, personal bests on both counts (b13, b14), and a 100 that beat his prior best there of 109 by nine. Resolution: in R4 he matched those figures exactly, 44 points and +27 again (b02, b03), survived quadruple-bogey 8s at the 6th and the SI-3 15th (b09, b06), drew level for the Trophy lead at the 14th — then bled 11 shots across 14-17 (b16) and settled for second and a personal-best gross total of +127 (b31).

discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Alex Baker's Opening 115 Cost Him the Trophy
discovered_storylines.standfirst: He set a new Royal Óbidos course-worst in Round 1, then matched personal bests of 44 points at Praia D'El Rey twice over — and was level for the lead with four holes remaining.

discovered_storylines.subject: The big-number ledger: Gregg Williams's 11 at the 7th, his 10 at the 9th, and a field that could not stop signing for nines
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Gregg Williams carded an 11 and a 10 in the same tournament and still recorded the best gross total of his career, which is the clearest measure of what the rest of his previous TEGs looked like.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: the defending Trophy champion opened at Royal Óbidos with a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 1st, added a sextuple-bogey 9 at the 15th (b35) and a 9 at the 18th (b42 for company from Jon Baker) — a round that cost him nothing much because everyone else was at it too. Turn: a sextuple-bogey 10 at the SI-4 9th in R2 (b28), a quadruple-bogey 7 at the 15th in R3 (b36), and then the centrepiece — 11 at the par-5 7th in R4 (b12), his worst hole relative to par on record. Resolution: none of it stopped a personal-best gross total of +115 (b32), while Jon Baker's quadruple-bogey 9 at the SI-1 17th in R4 (b05) and David Mullin's quintuple-bogey 9 at the 10th in R3 (b15) kept the ledger ticking over.

discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: An Eleven, a Ten and a Personal Best
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Gregg Williams took eleven shots at the 7th at Praia D'El Rey and still finished TEG 9 with the best gross total of his career — and he was far from the only man making a mess.

discovered_storylines.subject: Jon Baker leads after R1 with a personal best at Royal Óbidos, then loses his tournament in three holes on the same course
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: He recorded the best gross total of his career and a course personal best and came away with fourth in the Trophy and yet another Green Jacket runner-up finish.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: 89 gross at Royal Óbidos in R1, nine shots better than his previous best there, was enough to lead the Trophy by one despite a quadruple-bogey 9 at the last (b42). Turn: in R3 he took 16 points from the opening five holes (b22) and then played 10, 11 and 12 in double, quadruple and double — eight shots gone, three holes without a net par (b46, b48, b20) — leaving his front nine ten points clear of his back nine (b19). Resolution: a 9 at the SI-1 17th in R4 (b05) finished the argument; a career-best gross total of +77 (b33) bought him fourth in the Trophy and second in the Jacket once more.

discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Three Holes Undo Jon Baker at Royal Óbidos
discovered_storylines.standfirst: He led the TEG 9 Trophy after Round 1 with his best-ever score at the course, then dropped eight shots in three holes in Round 3 and never recovered his footing.

vehicle_fit_response.note: Taken up — Patterson's poor R3 into a best-in-field 47 (b45) is literally the mechanism of the win, and Alex Baker's course-worst 115 into twin personal bests is the report's strongest subplot; counterfactual rides alongside for the level-at-the-14th finish, inevitability for Mullin's wire-to-wire Jacket.'.'

why_the_champion_won: John Patterson built it: best-in-field rounds of 49 and 47 at Praia D'El Rey either side of a 34 in R3 that let Alex Baker level with four holes to play, beating Alex Baker head-to-head in three of the four rounds — and Alex Baker's own opening round at Royal Óbidos was so bad that a merely ordinary one in its place would have taken the Trophy off him.
